history.dynasty: Kachwaha (Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, founder of Jaipur)
history.period: 18th century, before the foundation of Jaipur (1727)
history.summary: NOT a duplicate: this is the 18th-century hilltop Ganesh shrine in the Aravalli hills near Nahargarh and Jaigarh forts, quite distinct from Moti Dungri Ganesh Temple (seq 2076). Built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II when he performed the Ashvamedha Yagya before laying the foundation stone of Jaipur. The temple's unique claim: it is said to be the only temple in the world where Ganesha is worshipped without a trunk, in the form of a small child known as Purushakriti (or Vigra Purushakriti). Tradition says the Maharaja had the idol placed so he could see it with binoculars from the Chandra Mahal of the City Palace. The shrine also holds idols of Riddhi and Siddhi, Ganesha's sons Shubh and Labh, and his mouse vehicle. Devotees climb 365 steps - symbolic of the days of the year - up the hill to reach it (approx. 500 ft elevation per one source; treat elevation figure as approximate). The temple is in the Nagara style; one source notes the 'Dhwajadheesh' Ganesha shrine of Bari-Chaupar is part of this temple's administration. Management rests with the 'Audichya' Brahmin family (the current priest reported as the 13th in line - single-source claim, verify). Note: local legend (the Parvati creating the child from her body's dirt, Shiva beheading him) is devotional folklore retold by travel sites, not history.

name: Garh Ganesh Temple
town: Jaipur (Brahmpuri, Aravalli hills near Nahargarh and Jaigarh forts)
town_description: Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan, is the 'Pink City' - founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, its rose-hued walled old city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the historic heart of Kachwaha Rajput culture, home to the City Palace, Hawa Mahal and Jantar Mantar. The Aravalli hills ringing the city hold the forts of Amber, Jaigarh and Nahargarh, with hilltop shrines like Garh Ganesh above the old city.

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport, about 10-12 km away (verify).
travel.railway: Jaipur Junction railway station, about 7 km away (jaipurexplore.com; verify).
travel.road: Near Gatore Ki Chhatriyan, Krishna Nagar, Brahmpuri (302002); reached by a 365-step climb up the hill - wear comfortable footwear. Buses and taxis run to the Brahmpuri base; the ascent is on foot.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Wednesdays have special significance but are busier. Early morning climbs are best.
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT (verify): jaipurexplore.com lists 7:30 AM-12:00 PM and 4:00 PM-8:00 PM all days; theunstumbled.com lists Mon/Tue/Thu-Sun 7:30 AM-12 PM and 4 PM-8:30 PM, and Wednesdays 6:30 AM-1 PM and 4 PM-10:30 PM. No entry fee.
